title: Nile Cruise Solo Traveller: Single Cabins, Supplements and Tips

Quick answer

Yes: a Nile cruise is one of the easiest Egypt trips for a solo traveller. Days come structured: a licensed guide, a small group of at most eight on Sawa departures, and meals on board. The one catch is cabin pricing. Most cruisers sell cabins for two, so booking alone usually triggers a single supplement, and there is no standard rate. On Sawa cruises the listed price is per traveller, and a solo cabin is confirmed in the booking, with no promise in advance on how it is arranged or priced, so check it for your date before you pay.

Travelling alone is the easy part, and Egypt does the rest. A Nile cruise packs the guide, the transport, the meals and a ready-made group onto one boat, which is why so many people take their first solo trip this way. Then the booking form asks the awkward question: price per person, based on two sharing. This post covers what a Nile cruise really costs alone, how the single supplement works, what the days feel like, and what to check before you book. Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure platform, lists live Nile departures.

Is a Nile cruise good for solo travellers?

Yes: a Nile cruise suits a solo traveller better than almost any other trip in Egypt. Every day is planned: a licensed guide leads the group to each temple, meals happen on board with the same faces, and the boat moves while you sleep. There is no transport to figure out and no evening left empty.

The honest catch is pricing, not company. Cruise cabins are sold for two, so travelling alone can trigger a single supplement: the one line in the budget to check before booking anything else. The rest of this post deals with exactly that.

How the single supplement on a Nile cruise works

A single supplement is the extra charge a cruise operator makes when one traveller occupies a cabin priced for two. Nile cruisers sell beds in pairs: the brochure fare assumes two people sharing, so a cabin taken alone is re-priced to recover the empty berth.

There is no universal percentage. Pure Nile Tours (updated 3 November 2026) notes that some operators publish a separate single fare, some add a percentage and some add a fixed amount, and advises asking for the total single-occupancy price for your exact ship, date and cabin. Get it in writing before booking flights.

On Sawa cruises the listed price is per traveller, and a solo cabin is confirmed in the booking, with no promise in advance. Check the cabin terms for your date before you pay. Reserving a seat is free, and nothing is charged until the date confirms.

Single cabins on Nile cruisers: what you can actually book

True single cabins are rare. Dedicated single cabins exist on only a limited number of ships; otherwise solo guests usually book a double or twin cabin for sole use, at a higher rate (Pure Nile Tours, November 2026). Boat assignments vary by date, so ask which cruiser your departure uses and whether it has single cabins before assuming the supplement applies. Dahabiyas, the wooden sailing boats with a handful of cabins, sharpen the same rule: fewer beds, so single occupancy is priced differently. Some are sold per cabin, some per person and some by private charter, and a whole cabin for one guest can be costly.

What a Nile cruise is like alone: day by day

On the water, solo cruising is social by day and quiet by night. On the four-night Nile Majesty 5-day cruise from Luxor, a solo traveller's days run like this, following the package's itinerary page:

  1. Day 1, Luxor. Airport pickup, lunch on board, Karnak with the group, then an evening horse-drawn carriage ride past the floodlit Luxor Temple. Your first evening is already planned.
  2. Day 2, West Bank. The Valley of the Kings, the Temple of Hatshepsut and the Colossi of Memnon; the boat sails south, leaving the deck chair and the riverbanks to you.
  3. Day 3, Edfu and Kom Ombo. The Temple of Horus at Edfu, then Kom Ombo, the riverside double temple of Sobek and Horus the Elder, and in the evening a felucca, a traditional wooden sailboat, around Kitchener's Island.
  4. Day 4, Aswan. Philae, the Temple of Isis, and the Aswan High Dam; the day closes with a sunset felucca sail.
  5. Day 5, Aswan. A last breakfast on the Nile, then a transfer to Aswan airport. Abu Simbel is not part of the cruise.

Who a solo cruise suits, and who it doesn't

Solo first-timers, travellers over fifty, and anyone who wants company without effort will settle in fast. It suits less well if you want nightlife (boats go quiet after dinner) or if you would rather have the days entirely to yourself; a land-based itinerary fits that better.

Is it safe to cruise the Nile alone?

For most solo travellers the boat is the calmest part of an Egypt trip: a staffed, contained place where your group of up to 8 sails on a shared five-star ship and does the excursions together with its guide, and dinner is a shared table. Excursions run as a group. In Luxor and Aswan towns, take the usual precautions: agree taxi fares or use the departure's transfers, dress modestly at temples, and keep valuables in the cabin safe. Sawa's WhatsApp line (+20 109 284 7613) is answered 24/7 while your tour is running. Check your government's travel advice before booking. The UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, in advice updated on 27 October 2026, does not advise against travel to Luxor or Aswan, but it warns of regional tensions linked to conflict in the Middle East and a risk of sudden escalation, and says travel against its advice can invalidate your insurance.

Nile cruise solo traveller costs: fare, supplement and extras

The fare is the floor, not the total. The four-night Nile Majesty costs from €610 per person: cabin on full board on a five-star cruiser, a licensed guide, the entrance tickets listed in the itinerary and a carriage ride (as listed in November 2026). The three-night Nile Discovery from Aswan starts from €500 and adds a licensed Egyptologist, a flight from Luxor to Cairo and a Cairo dinner cruise. What sits on top:

  • Drinks on board: full board covers meals, not drinks.
  • Tips: baksheesh, Egypt's customary tipping, for the guide and crew; the Sawa cruise pages list tips as not included. Carry small notes in cash.
  • Abu Simbel: not part of either cruise, and the cruises take no extensions; the separate Aswan to Abu Simbel day tour runs about 9 hours with hotel pickup in Aswan and 3.5 to 4 hours by road each way, from €50 per person (as listed in November 2026). As a day tour it carries no solo surcharge. Book flights only after each date confirms.
  • Travel insurance (listed as not included on the Nile Majesty), international flights and the Egyptian visa; most nationalities can apply on the official e-visa portal.
  • The single supplement itself, wherever one applies to a solo cabin.

Five ways solo travellers keep the total down:

  • Join a shared departure: the price is set per traveller, and you join a guided group of at most eight; check the solo cabin terms in the booking.
  • Ask whether the assigned cruiser has genuine single cabins: they are limited, so ask early.
  • Take the three-night Nile Discovery from €500 and put the saving toward Abu Simbel, remembering that it includes a domestic flight and a dinner cruise, so compare like with like.
  • Get the supplement in writing before booking flights; it moves a solo budget more than the boat's star rating does.
  • Travel in a quiet month, when operators may be more flexible, but get any waiver or discount in writing, because nothing is guaranteed.

How to do a solo Nile cruise with Sawa Tours

Sawa Tours is a shared-departure platform with a fixed catalogue: Sawa sets the calendar and the prices, and each departure is operated by one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date, named before the deposit is due. Sawa works with a founding operating partner, Capital Travel Service (licence 2179). Groups never exceed eight travellers, and when one fills, a new independent departure opens. Choose a forming date, or start your own, which Sawa's team reviews before it opens; reserving a seat is free, with no card. When the fourth traveller has reserved the date, it confirms (the GoAhead) and only then is payment taken: a 25% deposit, with the balance due 14 days before departure, by a secure payment link from Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241); charges are in euros. A cruise date must reach four by 30 days before; if it does not, it is cancelled, nothing is charged and another date is suggested. Cancel 30 or more days before and there is no charge; from 29 to 15 days you lose half the deposit (12.5%); at 14 days or fewer, or a no-show, the deposit (25%) is retained. Some components, such as flights and cabins, may become non-refundable earlier, and this is disclosed before payment. Once confirmed, a date is not cancelled for low numbers. The full detail is in Sawa's terms. Browse forming Nile cruise departures, read how Sawa works, or see how the GoAhead works.

The verdict for solo travellers

A Nile cruise is one of the easiest, most social ways to see Egypt alone: the structured days and small guided group do the work of company. The only real threat to the budget is the single supplement, so get the solo cabin terms confirmed before you pay. Browse forming Nile cruise departures on Sawa, or start your own date on the Nile Majesty cruise from Luxor: reserving a seat is free.

faq.q: How much is the single supplement on a Nile cruise?
faq.a: There is no standard figure: each operator, boat, cabin grade and season sets its own, as a separate single fare, a percentage or a fixed amount. Ask for the total single-occupancy price for your exact ship and date. On Sawa cruises (from €610 for the four-night sailing, as listed in November 2026) the solo cabin is confirmed in the booking, with no promise in advance, so check its terms before you pay.

faq.q: Do I have to share a cabin with a stranger on a Nile cruise?
faq.a: On most Nile cruisers, solo travellers take a cabin alone and the operator's single-supplement policy applies. Do not assume a company will pair you with a stranger; if you want that, ask about its matching rules and what happens if no match is found. On Sawa cruises the solo cabin is confirmed in the booking, with no promise in advance, so read what your booking confirms before you pay.

faq.q: Is Egypt safe for a woman travelling alone on a Nile cruise?
faq.a: Many women travel the Nile solo, and the cruise format works in their favour: a staffed boat, a licensed guide with the group on every excursion, and meals eaten aboard. Take normal precautions in town (agreed taxi fares, modest dress at temples, valuables in the cabin safe) and check your government's current travel advice before booking.

faq.q: Will I be the only solo traveller on the boat?
faq.a: You may not be, but nobody can promise who joins a date. A Sawa group is whoever reserves the date, from four to eight travellers, and the departures page shows how many have reserved. If no existing date suits you, start your own on the package page: Sawa reviews and opens it, and other travellers join until the fourth triggers the GoAhead.

faq.q: What happens if the departure doesn't fill?
faq.a: Nothing is charged until a date reaches four travellers and gets the GoAhead. If it does not reach four by 30 days before departure, the date is cancelled, you pay nothing, and Sawa suggests another date. Once a date is confirmed, it is not cancelled for low numbers, even if someone drops out.

faq.q: Is a three-night or four-night cruise better for solo travellers?
faq.a: The three-night Nile Discovery from Aswan (from €500) fits a short trip: Aswan's sights all land on the first day, and the package includes the flight on to Cairo and a Cairo dinner cruise. The four-night Nile Majesty from Luxor (from €610) spreads Luxor over two days, which means easier pacing and more deck time, and you finish in Aswan, the starting point for an Abu Simbel day tour.
